For my own curiosity, what is "older iOS"? 10? 12?
We have to figure that out. On macOS it was broken up to 10.14. If iOS was broken in the same timeframe that would point towards iOS 12 being the last broken version and iOS 13 the first fixed.
The Helix logs suggest the error happened on iOS 13.5 and tvOS 13.4. Locally I use iOS 14.5 simulator where the error doesn't happen.

Third option would be to do nothing and disable the test on !macOS and document it as a platform quirk for older platforms. Empty encryption / decryption in PKCS1 RSA seems... less likely to be demanded. The upshot being then we would not need to implement any of the PKCS padding ourselves.

That could at least be an interim step as well while the rest of the tests / functionality is brought up.

I am generally fine with having the quirk but there is prior precedent in implementing the RSA padding in managed code in RsaPaddingProcessor. In fact the same quirk exists on decryption and encryption and the encryption code path already has a workaround.

> here is prior precedent in implementing the RSA padding in managed code in RsaPaddingProcessor

My recollection is that we only do manual padding when encrypting empty, but that Windows decrypt-empty worked fine.

> Third option would be to do nothing and disable the test on !macOS and document it as a platform quirk for older platforms. 

If it was a server OS I'd be worried about some DOS-ability from that.  But for clients that concern doesn't really apply... and encrypting/decrypting nothing is obviously not very common (since both Windows and macOS/iOS have had boundary condition bugs on it).

Just documenting it as broken on older iOS-variants might be the way to go.  There's more compat wiggle room there, since the unified stack hasn't ever run on those OSes.  (Sure, regressing from Mono is unfortunate, but, there are probably a handful of papercuts already.)
Not sure how to disable the test for a specific version of iOS/tvOS, so keeping the active issue for now and pushing this to 7.0.0
